summary: Iteration 12 tested E1's Gemini-fallback contract on /api/chat/upload and /api/chat/stream. E1's code changes are CORRECT and the fallback path DOES execute at runtime (backend logs confirm the sequence: openai/gpt-5.4 fails → warning logged → gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview attempted → same error). HOWEVER the 3 Gemini-fallback assertions FAILED because Gemini itself also returns 'litellm.APIError: OpenAIException - Daily spend limit reached'. Root cause: the Emergent LLM proxy enforces ONE shared daily-spend budget across ALL providers on a given EMERGENT_LLM_KEY (sk-emergent-38dE3EcA56e3d681e3). Both openai/gpt-5.4 AND gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview route through the same proxy under the same key, so when the daily budget is exhausted, EVERY provider is exhausted. Regression: /api/chat/models (4 items), /api/whatsapp/config (missing key present), /api/media/ensure-ambient (200) all PASSED. Frontend re-testing was skipped because backend proof (both providers 409) makes it deterministic that the frontend will still show the canned '…interrumpió mi voz…' fallback — no code change on the frontend can rescue this until the key's daily budget resets or is topped up. 3 passed, 3 failed in test_iter12_gemini_fallback.py (the 3 failures are all quota-caused, not code-caused).

minor.issue: Elena reaction is still the canned 'Mmm mi amor, no me llegó bien tu foto…' fallback. E1's Gemini fallback code IS invoked (logs show 'Elena upload-reaction primary failed …; falling back to Gemini.'), but Gemini also raises 'Daily spend limit reached' because it shares the same EMERGENT_LLM_KEY budget as OpenAI. Endpoint still returns 200 with valid schema — contract holds; only content is degraded.

Same root cause. Logs show: 'Chat stream primary (openai/gpt-5.4) failed …; falling back to Gemini.' then 'Gemini fallback also failed'. Stream emits event:user, event:start, one event:delta with the canned string, event:done. Contract holds; only content is degraded.

Even a direct call with chat_provider=gemini, chat_model=gemini-3-flash-preview returns the canned '…interrumpió mi voz…' fallback because the Gemini call itself throws daily_limit_reached from the Emergent proxy. This CONFIRMS the shared-budget theory: it is NOT specific to the openai→gemini fallback path — Gemini in isolation is also blocked.

SHARED-KEY ARCHITECTURAL CONCERN: Because both DEFAULT_CHAT_PROVIDER (openai) and the fallback (gemini) authenticate with the SAME EMERGENT_LLM_KEY through the SAME Emergent proxy, the fallback provides ZERO isolation against a proxy-level daily_limit_reached response. If true failover is desired, the fallback needs to use either (a) a different API key, (b) a direct-to-Gemini SDK bypassing the Emergent proxy, or (c) accept that this is a graceful-degradation-only fallback for provider-specific outages, NOT for shared-quota exhaustion.

rca of the issue: Both /api/chat/upload and /api/chat/stream return canned Spanish fallback strings because EMERGENT_LLM_KEY sk-emergent-38dE3EcA56e3d681e3 has exhausted its daily spend budget at the Emergent proxy level. The proxy enforces the budget UNIFORMLY across every underlying provider (openai/gpt-5.4, gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview, etc.), so E1's Gemini-fallback (although correctly implemented and correctly invoked at runtime — verified in supervisor error log) hits the exact same 409 daily_limit_reached error as the primary.
